setup: Choose a trail or hill route that suits your fitness, and wear shoes with grip and ankle support for the ground you expect.
Stand tall with a light pack settled close to your back, straps snug, and your eyes on the path a few metres ahead.
steps: Walk at a pace you can hold for the whole route, shortening your stride and leaning slightly into the slope on climbs.
Push off the whole foot and drive through the glutes and thighs on each uphill step, keeping a steady rhythm.
On descents, bend the knees a little, land softly, and let your arms balance you over loose or uneven ground.
Keep moving at a steady effort, stopping only as the route or terrain demands, until the planned distance or time is done.
instructions.breathing: Breathe deeply in time with your steps; slow the pace rather than hold your breath when a climb gets hard.

common_faults.fault: Starting too fast and fading before the end of the route
common_faults.correction: Settle into a pace you could talk at and save any push for the final stretch.

common_faults.fault: Locking the knees and landing heavily on descents
common_faults.correction: Keep the knees slightly bent and take shorter, quieter steps so the thighs absorb each landing.

common_faults.fault: Hunching under a pack and staring at your feet
common_faults.correction: Tighten the straps so the load sits close, lift your chest, and look a few metres ahead.

precautions: Carry water, check the weather and daylight before setting out, and tell someone your route and expected return.
Build up distance and elevation gradually, since downhill walking loads the knees and thighs more than flat ground.

name: Hiking
summary: Sustained walking over trails and hills, where climbs and descents ask more of the glutes and thighs than walking on the flat.
